questions.question: What is the maximum permitted length of a purpose-made tow rope?
options: 3 metres
5 metres
8 metres
10 metres
questions.explanation: A longer rope gives the towed car too much room to swing out or run into the towing car, so the length is capped by law.

questions.question: How fast may the two cars drive when one is being towed on a tow rope?
options: No faster than 20 km/h
No faster than 30 km/h
No faster than 45 km/h
No faster than 60 km/h
questions.explanation: The towed car's stopping distance is limited by the rope, so both drivers must hold a low and as constant a speed as possible.

questions.question: In which gear position must a car with automatic transmission be while it is towed?
options: Park
Drive
Neutral
Reverse
questions.explanation: An automatic gearbox is not lubricated properly when the engine is off, so any driven position can wreck it; the tow must also be short and slow.

questions.question: The anti-lock brake warning light comes on while you are driving. What does it mean?
options: The braking system has failed and the car must not be driven at all
The brake fluid has dropped below its minimum permitted level
The anti-lock function is off, but ordinary braking usually still works
The parking brake has been left partly applied while driving
questions.explanation: The lamp reports only the loss of the anti-lock function; the hydraulic braking circuit is separate and has its own warning light.

questions.question: The rear fog beam indicator is lit on your dashboard. Where must you switch that lamp off?
options: In urban areas
On gravel roads
Inside tunnels
On mountain roads
questions.explanation: The rear fog lamp is far brighter than a tail light and dazzles the driver behind, which is why an indicator on the dashboard reminds you it is on.

questions.question: The oil pressure warning light comes on while driving. What should you do first?
options: Drive slowly onward to the nearest automobile repair shop
Pour in more oil straight away with the engine idling
Read the dipstick while the engine is still running
Stop the engine at once and let it cool before checking
questions.explanation: Low oil pressure can destroy an engine within moments, and the oil must settle back into the sump before a dipstick reading means anything.

questions.question: After an oil pressure warning, the dipstick shows a normal oil level. What now?
options: Restart the engine and drive gently back home
Leave the engine off until the cause has been found
Add more oil anyway and carry on driving
Restart the engine after an hour of cooling
questions.explanation: A normal level means the fault lies somewhere else and is probably far more serious, so starting the engine again is likely to damage it.

questions.question: What supplies the electricity for the lamps and radio while the engine is running?
options: The battery
The starter motor
The ignition coil
The alternator
questions.explanation: The battery's job is to power the electrics with the engine off; once the engine runs, the alternator takes over and recharges the battery as well.

questions.question: What happens if the serpentine belt breaks while you are driving?
options: The engine loses its oil pressure and seizes almost at once
The brakes lose their power assistance within a few seconds
Nothing is noticed until the next attempt to start the car
The battery stops charging and the car eventually stops running
questions.explanation: The belt drives the alternator, so the car runs on the battery alone until it is flat; the battery warning light comes on to signal this.

questions.question: Which is the recommended way to get a car going when its battery is dead?
options: Push-start it with the help of another vehicle
Tow-start it in a high gear on a quiet road
Jump-start it with jumper cables from another car
Roll-start it down a slope in second gear
questions.explanation: Push- and tow-starting keep two vehicles moving very close together, and the probability of a collision during the manoeuvre is substantial.

questions.question: Which jumper cable connection is made first when jump-starting a car?
options: The red clamp on the dead battery's positive terminal
The red clamp on the good battery's positive terminal
The black clamp on the good battery's negative terminal
The black clamp on the dead battery's negative terminal
questions.explanation: The sequence works through the two positive terminals before the two negative ones, and the flat battery's negative post is connected last of all.

questions.question: Why must you never open the coolant reservoir lid on a hot engine?
options: Cold air rushing in can crack the hot radiator
The coolant instantly loses its antifreeze effect
Dirt getting in will block the radiator at once
Boiling coolant can spurt out of the opening
questions.explanation: The cooling system is under pressure when hot, so releasing the cap lets the fluid flash into steam and scald whoever is standing over it.

questions.question: Why should you keep your face away from a battery while connecting jumper cables?
options: The alternator may be ruined by the sudden current surge
The battery itself may explode, especially if sparks fly
The cables can melt and weld themselves to the terminals
The engine management system may be reset by the sparks
questions.explanation: A battery gives off gas that a spark at the terminal can ignite; if acid does reach the face it must be rinsed at once with plenty of water.

questions.question: What must never be used to put out a burning gasoline fire?
options: A dry chemical extinguisher
A blanket thrown over it
Dry sand shovelled onto it
Water or any other liquid
questions.explanation: Burning petrol floats on top and is carried along by the liquid, so the fire is spread rather than smothered.

questions.question: What makes the carbon monoxide in exhaust fumes so hard to detect?
options: It has neither colour nor smell of any kind
It has a sharp smell that quickly numbs the nose
It is heavier than air and pools near the ground
It stings the eyes only long after it has harmed you
questions.explanation: The victim gets no warning while the gas binds to haemoglobin and blocks oxygen from reaching the tissues, which is why an engine must never run in a closed space.

questions.question: What hazard does a catalytic converter present to the car and its surroundings?
options: It leaks carbon monoxide straight into the passenger cabin
It gets extremely hot and can set flammable material alight
It stops working completely once the engine has warmed up
It makes the exhaust fumes considerably more toxic than before
questions.explanation: The converter only cleans the exhaust once it reaches a high working temperature, so parking over dry grass or leaves is a real fire risk.

questions.question: How should the pedals be operated in a car with automatic transmission?
options: With the right foot on gas, the left on brake
With whichever foot happens to be comfortable
With the right foot only, for both pedals
With the left foot only, resting on the brake
questions.explanation: There is no clutch pedal to occupy the left foot, and using both feet risks pressing the accelerator and the brake at the same time.

questions.question: What are the consequences of running a tire at too low an air pressure?
options: Fuel consumption rises and the tire loses grip
Fuel consumption falls but the tread wears faster
Grip improves although the steering grows heavier
Nothing changes until the tire is almost flat
questions.explanation: An under-inflated tire deforms as it rolls, which increases rolling resistance and distorts the patch of rubber that touches the road.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread groove depth required during winter, 1 November to 14 April?
options: 3 mm
1.6 mm
5 mm
8 mm
questions.explanation: The year-round minimum is only 1.6 mm, but winter conditions need deeper grooves to clear away snow, slush and water.

questions.question: What is the usual recommended maximum speed when driving on a compact spare tire?
options: 50 km/h
90 km/h
80 km/h
100 km/h
questions.explanation: The compact spare is deliberately made smaller and lighter to save space and cost, so it is only meant for a short trip to a repair shop.
